topStories.headline: Red Oak Council Approves Compass Data Center Expansion to Nearly 900 Acres
topStories.dek: A divided council voted 4-1 Tuesday to let Compass Datacenters add roughly 100 acres to its already-approved Red Oak project, over loud objections from residents who say the facility will drive up utility bills and bring unwanted noise.
topStories.body:
The Red Oak City Council and its Planning and Zoning Commission held a joint session on Tuesday, November 17, to consider whether Compass Datacenters should be allowed to expand its approved campus on Oglesby Road. After presentations by city staff and company officials — who said design changes had been made in response to community concerns raised over the past several months — the council voted 4-1 to approve the rezoning, bringing the total footprint to nearly 900 acres.

Opponents packed the chambers wearing protest buttons and submitted public comment forms, arguing that a development of this size would strain the city's water and electricity infrastructure, generate persistent industrial noise, and alter the rural character of southeast Ellis County. Supporters of the project — some wearing red shirts — declined to speak on camera after the meeting.

The original 800-acre project had been approved in May and remains under a court challenge filed by residents. Tuesday's vote adds acreage to that contested approval, meaning both the underlying permit and the expansion now face potential legal scrutiny.

Compass officials showed updated site plans during the meeting, which they said incorporated feedback gathered at a well-attended community open house earlier this month. City leaders have pointed to the project as a potential economic engine for a city that has historically had a limited commercial tax base.

The group Red Oak Say No More Data Center said before the meeting that residents felt shut out of a process that could fundamentally reshape their community. With the court challenge still active and the expansion now approved, the dispute over the future of Red Oak's agricultural fringe shows no sign of resolution.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Council Turns Down Second Walmart After Marathon Session
topStories.dek: Following three hours of public comment and council debate, Midlothian councilmembers denied a rezoning request that would have cleared the way for a second Walmart superstore in the city.
topStories.body:
Midlothian's City Council wrapped up a lengthy November 18 meeting by voting to deny the rezoning of a 55.708-acre site at the northeast corner of South Walnut Grove Road and U.S. Highway 287. The applicant had sought a planned-development designation to allow a Walmart signature supercenter — described in earlier filings as a roughly 182,000-square-foot store featuring a drone delivery concept — along with associated mixed-use development.

The public hearing had been tabled multiple times since it first appeared on the council agenda in October, most recently at the applicant's request until the November 10 meeting before being pushed again to November 18. By the time the council took the final vote, councilmembers had heard extensive comment from residents on both sides of the question.

Midlothian already has one Walmart on U.S. 287. Opponents of the second store raised concerns about traffic on the already-busy corridor, the impact on existing small businesses, and whether the site's land-use designation aligned with the city's long-term comprehensive plan.

The denial puts the project on hold, though applicants in Midlothian zoning cases may generally return to the council with a revised proposal at a future date.

topStories.headline: Hawks Survive Bi-District Thriller, Take on Longview Tonight in Area Round
topStories.dek: Red Oak edged Killeen Harker Heights 31-27 last Friday to advance in the 6A Division II playoffs, and the Hawks face Longview at 7 p.m. tonight at Kincaide Stadium in Dallas.
topStories.body:
Red Oak's football team delivered one of the more improbable results of the first round of the UIL Class 6A Division II playoffs, holding off Killeen Harker Heights 31-27 at Leo Buckley Stadium on November 13. Running back Daylan Johnson was the standout performer, rushing for 188 yards and three touchdowns on 15 carries, including an 81-yard burst that effectively sealed the outcome. Quarterback Tuhran Square II added 125 passing yards and a score.

The victory was notable for more reasons than the score. Dave Campbell's Texas Football had picked the Hawks to finish second-to-last in District 11-6A — a division that includes powerhouses Waxahachie, North Crowley, and Duncanville. The team played every regular-season game on the road this fall while its stadium underwent renovations, and it entered the playoffs having moved up a full classification from Class 5A. Despite all of that, the Hawks finished the regular season with enough wins to qualify, then knocked off a Harker Heights squad that fought back gamely behind receiver Ryan Taylor (182 yards, two touchdowns) and rusher Brandon Fowlkes Jr. (151 yards, one score).

Red Oak now faces Longview (10-1) in the area round tonight, Friday, November 20, at 7 p.m. at Kincaide Stadium in Dallas. Longview handled Garland Rowlett 42-20 in the bi-district round. A win tonight would push the Hawks into the regional round the week of November 26-28.

moreNews.headline: Midlothian Voters Reject All Five Bond Propositions Totaling $192 Million
moreNews.body: On November 3, Midlothian residents voted down all five propositions in the city's 2026 bond referendum by margins of more than 60 percent against on each measure. The package had included $102.3 million for street improvements, $6.8 million for a new police substation, $10 million for drainage projects, $47.3 million for existing park upgrades, and $26.1 million for two new parks — a combined $192 million that city officials had said could be issued without raising the tax rate. The outcome mirrored a statewide trend on November 3, when Texas voters rejected roughly 75 percent of bond and tax-rate measures on local ballots across the state.

moreNews.headline: TSTC Red Oak Campus Lands $2 Million Federal Grant for Mobile Manufacturing Lab
moreNews.body: Texas State Technical College's North Texas campus in Red Oak announced on November 17 that it has received a $2 million Economic Development Administration Disaster Supplemental grant. Combined with a $500,000 campus match, the funds will be used to build and deploy a mobile Advanced Manufacturing training lab that will travel to industry partners across the region. The campus became eligible for the EDA grant after both Ellis and Denton counties were declared federal disaster areas following severe storms in May 2024. Industry partners including Amber Electrical Contractors, Lippert University, and Mary Kay provided letters of support for the application.

moreNews.headline: Two Men Charged in 2025 Midlothian Arson That Targeted Sleeping Family
moreNews.body: Midlothian police announced on November 10 the arrests of Rashad Gilbert Harrington, 27, of DeSoto, and Bennie Leon McGriff Jr., 55, of Kerens, in connection with an August 2025 arson at a home on McAlpin Road. Investigators say Harrington poured an ignitable liquid around the front of the house and set it alight while the Wilson family slept inside; a daughter who was still awake spotted the flames and alerted the family. DNA found on a gas can nozzle left in a flower bed matched Harrington in October 2026 crime lab testing, and cell phone records and Flock camera footage linked McGriff as the alleged driver. Both men face first-degree felony arson-of-a-habitation charges. Police said the investigation remains active and that a motive has not been publicly established.
